text: How many layers are in the OSI Model and the TCP/IP Protocol Suite (based on this chapter), respectively?
info: OSI = 7 Layers, TCP/IP = 5 Layers (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Application).

text: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the TCP/IP Protocol Suite and the OSI Model?
info: Bottom 4 layers (Physical to Transport) are identical in both models.

answers.text: TCP/IP was developed after the OSI Model
The lower 4 layers of TCP/IP match the lower 4 layers of the OSI Model
TCP/IP splits its top layer into Presentation and Session layers
The OSI Model is practical while TCP/IP is purely theoretical

text: The Application Layer in TCP/IP covers which layers of the OSI Model?
info: TCP/IP combines OSI's top 3 layers (L5, L6, L7) into a single Application Layer.

text: What is the main responsibility of the Application Layer in the OSI Model?

answers.text: To translate, encrypt, and compress data
To allow access to network resources
To establish, manage, and terminate sessions

text: Which layer of the OSI Model is responsible for data translation, encryption, and compression?
What is the primary function of the Session Layer in the OSI Model?

answers.text: To establish, manage, and terminate sessions
To move packets from source to destination

What is the primary function of the Physical Layer in the OSI Model?
info: Physical = Bits + Transmission Medium + Electrical/Mechanical specs.

answers.text: To transmit bits over a medium; to provide mechanical and electrical specifications

text: Which statement is TRUE regarding the Physical and Data Link Layers in the TCP/IP suite?

answers.text: TCP/IP defines its own unique protocols for the Physical Layer
TCP/IP supports open standard protocols only

text: What does "Best-effort delivery service" mean in the context of the IP protocol?
info: Best-effort = Tries hard, but NO error checking/tracking.

answers.text: Makes its best attempt to deliver packets, but provides no error checking or tracking

text: Why was IP designed to be Unreliable and Connectionless?
info: IP stays fast & simple -> TCP handles reliability.

answers.text: To maximize transmission speed, leaving reliability control to the Transport Layer (TCP)
Because error-checking code could not be written at the time
It was an initial design oversight

text: How many main supporting protocols exist at the Network Layer according to this chapter?
info: 4 Supporting protocols = ARP, RARP, ICMP, IGMP.

info: UDP operates at the Transport Layer (Layer 4).

info: Router reads IP Addresses to perform Routing.

text: What is the function of the ARP (Address Resolution Protocol)?

answers.text: Translates MAC Address to IP Address
Translates IP Address to Physical Address (MAC Address)

text: Why is ARP necessary when transmitting data within a Local Area Network (LAN)?
info: LAN frames require Physical Addresses for delivery.

answers.text: Because IP addresses cannot function on LANs
Because physical data transmission in a LAN requires a Physical (MAC) Address

text: How does RARP (Reverse Address Resolution Protocol) differ from ARP?

answers.text: Finds IP Address using a Physical Address
Finds Port Number using an IP Address
Finds MAC Address using an IP Address
Translates Domain Name to IP Address

text: In which situation is RARP typically used?
info: RARP = Diskless host retrieving its IP upon boot.

answers.text: Sending an email to a peer
Booting up a Diskless Computer for the first time

text: What is the primary role of ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol)?

answers.text: Sends error notification messages back to the source when datagram issues occur
Maps IP address to MAC address

text: What are the two main categories of ICMP messages?
Which protocol does the ping command rely on?
info: ping command uses ICMP Echo Request/Reply.

text: What is the purpose of IGMP (Internet Group Message Protocol)?

answers.text: Facilitates sending messages to a group of recipients simultaneously (Multicast)
Sends error notifications back to the sender
Assigns IP addresses to client devices

text: Which pair correctly matches the protocol with its core function?
info: ICMP handles diagnostic and error reporting.

text: If a host needs to determine the MAC address corresponding to IP 192.168.1.50, which protocol will be invoked?
info: Know IP, want MAC -> Use ARP.

text: What is a major difference between TCP and UDP?
info: TCP retransmits lost segments; UDP sends and forgets.

answers.text: TCP is process-to-process, whereas UDP is host-to-host
TCP includes a retransmission mechanism for lost packets, whereas UDP does not
UDP has a larger header size than TCP

text: Why is an Internet Address (IP Address) needed when Physical Addresses already exist?
info: IP = Universal addressing system connecting diverse physical networks.

answers.text: Physical Addresses cannot cross heterogeneous networks, necessitating a Universal Addressing system

text: What happens to IP and Physical addresses as a packet travels across multiple router hops?

Both IP and Physical addresses change at each hop

text: Each dot-separated number in an IPv4 address represents how many bytes, and what is its maximum value?
info: Each octet = 1 Byte (8 bits) -> Range 0 to 255.
